content.thinking: I need to fix several range phrasings - several "Over" instances need checking, and "Up to" should become "Over" for consistency. The single-minute case should just use "At" instead of "In the minute."

action_items.item: Roll out io-shop feature flag changes in production in stages, starting with a small share of traffic.
Halt and revert an io-shop flag rollout automatically when the account-page error rate rises above its baseline during the rollout.
Require tests that exercise a flag-gated code path with the flag on before that flag can be switched on in production.
Review the other per-month figures in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py for divisions by a count that can be empty in a month.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The share of requests that failed rose from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_while_broken} while it was broken, and peaked at {errors_at_worst}. The service's own account-page error warnings were highest at {Gbac1.7}.
Over {G5309.3}, account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at line {F1.1} of src/io_shop/spend_summary.py.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: the production change events read for the day before the onset returned only the flag change and no deploys. At {T10.1}, every replica ran a single revision.
Another flag change: at {T16.1}, the flag provider's history for the hour before showed only one flag change by anyone but Argus, which was this one.
Shoppers closing the connection: these ClientDisconnected failures were logged over {G46bc.3}, starting well before the onset, while the metrics read showed the service at its baseline error rate.

causal_chain.step: The new spend summary code path was running because an admin switched on the feature flag monthly-spend-feature at {P1.1}. Over {G7e5d.4}, every flag evaluation was off. At {G971b.6}, evaluations split {G971b.2} on and {G971b.1} off, and over {Gce95.4} every evaluation was on. Switching the flag off at {T19.1} brought the service back to normal by {T21.2}, and the action was judged confirmed at {T22.1}.

According to Code-Fix's reading of the source, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` divides `account.total_this_month_cents` by `len(bought_this_month)` without checking that the list is non-empty. For a shopper who has bought before but not in the current month, that list is empty, so the function raises ZeroDivisionError.

The check is missing because the reasoning behind the lifetime average was carried over to the month. The lifetime average's docstring says its divisor is empty only for an account that never bought anything, which no real shopper is. That does not hold for a single month, where an empty divisor is common.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary on shoppers' account pages exposed a calculation that likely divides by the number of purchases a shopper made this month without allowing for shoppers who bought nothing this month, so their account pages failed.

contributing_factors.factor: The flag change reached every evaluation within moments: first a split between on and off, then on for all. No staged rollout and no automatic halt on a rising error rate were seen for the flag change.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout that halts on a rising account-page error rate would have exposed only a small share of shoppers and stopped or reverted the flag before most account pages failed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that runs the monthly spend path for a shopper who has earlier purchases but none this month, even though the test file Code-Fix read calls this kind of shopper the ordinary case. Code-Fix's new tests for that case are written to raise ZeroDivisionError against the current code.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test of this case would have failed before the flag was switched on, so the fault would have been found without any shopper seeing it.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well: The Investigator tied the onset to the flag change by matching the flag-evaluation log lines, which switched from off to on, against the ZeroDivisionError lines that began in the same minute.
Argus switched monthly-spend-feature off {T19.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Argus confirmed {T22.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised that switching off the flag had brought the service back.
Code-Fix proposed a fix, with tests, as draft pull request PR #361.
went_wrong: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to the alert, so no person was told while the incident ran.

input.root_cause: The monthly spend summary path that monthly-spend-feature turns on calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's total by the number of purchases made this month and never checks whether there were any. So for any shopper who has bought before but not this month, it raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1} and their account page fails. The check is missing because the reasoning behind the lifetime average was carried over to a single month: the lifetime divisor is empty only for an account that never bought anything, but a month's divisor is often empty.
input.still_at_risk: The flag is off, but the faulty monthly spend calculation is still in the code, so switching monthly-spend-feature back on would likely make account pages fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
